task_prompts.chi-middleware--nosniff:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.NoSniff(next http.Handler) http.Handler`, which sets the `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` response header on every response.

Examples:
- `GET /` -> `200` (reaches the next handler), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `POST /upload` -> `200` (reaches the next handler), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--allow-methods:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.AllowMethods(methods ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `405 Method Not Allowed`, with an `Allow` header listing the allowed methods (comma-separated, in the order given), to requests whose method is not one of `methods`; other requests reach the next handler.

Examples with `AllowMethods("GET", "POST")`:
- `GET /a` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `DELETE /a` -> `405`, `Allow: GET, POST`
- `POST /a` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--hsts:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.HSTS(maxAge time.Duration, includeSubdomains bool) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which sets the `Strict-Transport-Security` response header to `max-age=<seconds>`, followed by `; includeSubDomains` when `includeSubdomains` is true.

Examples:
- `HSTS(24*time.Hour, false)`: `GET /` -> `200` (reaches the next handler), `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=86400`
- `HSTS(time.Hour, true)`: `GET /` -> `200` (reaches the next handler), `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=3600; includeSubDomains`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--require-header:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.RequireHeader(name string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `400 Bad Request` to requests that do not carry the request header `name`, or carry it empty; other requests reach the next handler.

Examples with `RequireHeader("X-Tenant")`:
- `GET /` with `X-Tenant: acme` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` -> `400`
- `GET /` with an empty `X-Tenant` -> `400`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--method-override:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.MethodOverride(next http.Handler) http.Handler`, which lets a `POST` request override its method with the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` request header: when the header is `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` (case-insensitive), the next handler sees that method, upper-cased. Any other method or header value is left unchanged.

Examples:
- `POST /items` with `X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE` -> the next handler sees method `DELETE`
- `POST /items` with `X-HTTP-Method-Override: patch` -> the next handler sees method `PATCH`
- `GET /items` with `X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE` -> the next handler sees method `GET`
- `POST /items` with `X-HTTP-Method-Override: TRACE` -> the next handler sees method `POST`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--allow-hosts:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.AllowHosts(hosts ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `403 Forbidden` to requests whose `Host`, without the port and compared case-insensitively, is not one of `hosts`; other requests reach the next handler.

Examples with `AllowHosts("example.com", "api.example.com")`:
- `GET /` with `Host: example.com` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` with `Host: API.Example.com:8080` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` with `Host: evil.com` -> `403`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--lowercase-path:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.LowercasePath(next http.Handler) http.Handler`, which lower-cases the request's URL path (`r.URL.Path`, and `r.URL.RawPath` when it is set) before the next handler sees it; the query string is left as it is.

Examples:
- `GET /Users/ABC?Q=1` -> the next handler sees path `/users/abc`, query `Q=1`
- `GET /already/lower` -> the next handler sees path `/already/lower`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--block-user-agents:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.BlockUserAgents(substrings ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `403 Forbidden` to requests whose `User-Agent` contains any of `substrings`, compared case-insensitively; requests without a User-Agent, and all others, reach the next handler.

Examples with `BlockUserAgents("curl", "BadBot")`:
- `GET /` with `User-Agent: curl/8.0` -> `403`
- `GET /` with `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; badbot/1.2)` -> `403`
- `GET /` with `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--api-key:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.APIKey(header string, keys ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `401 Unauthorized` to requests whose request header `header` is not exactly one of `keys` (a missing header included); other requests reach the next handler.

Examples with `APIKey("X-API-Key", "k1", "k2")`:
- `GET /` with `X-API-Key: k2` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` with `X-API-Key: K2` -> `401`
- `GET /` -> `401`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--vary:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.Vary(headers ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which adds each of `headers` to the response's `Vary` header, keeping the `Vary` values the response already has.

Examples with `Vary("Accept-Encoding", "Origin")`:
- `GET /` -> `200` (reaches the next handler), `Vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin`

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--content-length-required:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.ContentLengthRequired(next http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `411 Length Required` to `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` requests whose body length is unknown (`r.ContentLength == -1`, as for a chunked body); other requests reach the next handler.

Examples:
- `POST /` with a body of unknown length -> `411`
- `PUT /` with a body of unknown length -> `411`
- `POST /` with the body `hello` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` with a body of unknown length -> `200` (reaches the next handler)

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
task_prompts.chi-middleware--max-header-count:
Add a new middleware to chi's middleware package: `middleware.MaxHeaderCount(n int) func(http.Handler) http.Handler`, which responds `431 Request Header Fields Too Large` to requests that carry more than `n` header fields (counted as distinct names in `r.Header`); other requests reach the next handler.

Examples with `MaxHeaderCount(2)`:
- `GET /` with `A: 1`, `B: 2` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)
- `GET /` with `A: 1`, `B: 2`, `C: 3` -> `431`
- `GET /` -> `200` (reaches the next handler)

Include tests, and document it in the README's list of middlewares, as the project does for its other middlewares.
